Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent registry is the Commercial Registry of the province where the registered office is located (Registro Mercantil Provincial), with prior name-clearance by the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).

Governing statute

Spanish Companies Law (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4, 20-23, 28-30, 32-35, 58-62, 159-204, 209-252, and 285-290; supplemented by the Commercial Registry Regulations (Real Decreto 1784/1996) and Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and CIRCE procedures.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the company bylaws and the required tax identification documentation.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 56 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid upon incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No general statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate of deposit may be used where the notary requires evidence of cash contribution. The amount shown is zero because Spain has no single fixed national state filing fee; notarial, registry, publication, municipal, and professional charges are variable.

Funding & unlock path: Before occupation, verify municipal fire-safety and accessibility requirements, obtain any required responsible declaration or technical certificate, and ensure the premises satisfy the Spanish Building Code and applicable fire-protection rules. Structural load certification is required where the premises contain server equipment, storage, or alterations affecting loads. Implement occupational risk prevention, emergency planning, electrical safety, and workplace health measures under Law 31/1995 and related regulations.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid upon incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No general statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate of deposit may be used where the notary requires evidence of cash contribution. The amount shown is zero because Spain has no single fixed national state filing fee; notarial, registry, publication, municipal, and professional charges are variable.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and ratifies the subscription and full payment of its issued shares by the founding shareholder as recorded in the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted for all statutory purposes; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if a board structure is adopted, [names] are appointed directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal incompatibility; (4) [name] is appointed managing officer with authority to complete tax, banking, registry, employment, data-protection, and operational registrations; and (5) the officers are authorized to execute all ancillary documents.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

No sector-specific industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for a consumer polling and cross-border market research SaaS platform. Premises-related controls are administered by the competent autonomous-community authority and the municipality where the office or technical installation is located.

Category: No manufacturing or sector operating permit is ordinarily required. A municipal responsible declaration for the opening or commencement of a non-industrial office activity, or a municipal activity licence where required by local rules, may be necessary.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Provincial and regional tax bodies have no corporate tax competence; the Basque Country and Navarra operate separate foral regimes only for entities with principal establishments there.

E-government filing portal

Step 1 - Obtain a provisional NIF for the company from AEAT using Modelo 036 before executing the incorporation deed. Step 2 - Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary and file the deed with the Registro Mercantil. Step 3 - Within one month of incorporation, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive corporate NIF (NIF-CIF) and simultaneously register for IVA (VAT) and IAE. Step 4 - Non-resident shareholders/parent entities must obtain their own non-resident NIF via Modelo 036/030 and, if applicable, appoint a Spanish tax representative. Step 5 - Deliver the ultimate beneficial owner declaration and maintain a local registered office and a Spanish bank account; if the SL is in a regulated sector, certifications are filed with the tax or supervisory authority as required.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is tax-resident under art. 8 LIS because it is incorporated under Spanish law. Worldwide income is subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT); general rate 25%; newly created trading entities may apply 15% to profits of the first two tax periods under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through election exists in Spanish domestic law; the entity is treated as a separate taxable person for CIT and IVA. Territorial_Scope: worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit; not a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity unless specifically authorised in the Zona Especial Canaria. — Step 1 - Obtain a provisional NIF for the company from AEAT using Modelo 036 before executing the incorporation deed. Step 2 - Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary and file the deed with the Registro Mercantil. Step 3 - Within one month of incorporation, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive corporate NIF (NIF-CIF) and simultaneously register for IVA (VAT) and IAE. Step 4 - Non-resident shareholders/parent entities must obtain their own non-resident NIF via Modelo 036/030 and, if applicable, appoint a Spanish tax representative. Step 5 - Deliver the ultimate beneficial owner declaration and maintain a local registered office and a Spanish bank account; if the SL is in a regulated sector, certifications are filed with the tax or supervisory authority as required.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is tax-resident under art. 8 LIS because it is incorporated under Spanish law. Worldwide income is subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT); general rate 25%; newly created trading entities may apply 15% to profits of the first two tax periods under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through election exists in Spanish domestic law; the entity is treated as a separate taxable person for CIT and IVA. Territorial_Scope: worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit; not a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity unless specifically authorised in the Zona Especial Canaria.

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box election. Available elections: (i) consolidated tax group regime (arts. 64-70 LIS) for resident groups with direct/indirect holding of at least 70% and unanimous shareholder election; (ii) reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created trading entities in the first two profitable periods; (iii) corporate tax credits for R&D+i and employment; (iv) ETVE holding company regime for EU/third-country shareholding management; (v) voluntary SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) filing; (vi) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) election for intra-EU distance sales and B2C digital services under the EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold; (vii) anti-hybrid rules under art. 15 LIS apply mandatorily to neutralise mismatches, with no domestic hybrid election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover threshold: any business habitually carrying out taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register for IVA before commencing activity. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C telecommunications/broadcasting/digital services supplied from Spain, the OSS registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (below the threshold, supplies remain taxable in the Member State of establishment). The Régimen Simplificado is available to small traders with turnover below EUR 250,000 but does not waive registration.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods are zero-rated under art. 21 LIVA if the goods physically leave EU customs territory and the exporter is the Spanish entity. For the market research/SaaS platform, exports of services to non-Spanish taxable persons (B2B) are outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rule (art. 69 LIVA); services to non-EU non-taxable persons (B2C) are also outside the scope when effectively used in a third country. Zero-rating under arts. 21-22 LIVA applies to services directly linked to exported goods and to certain international services. The SL must substantiate the customer's status and country, the nature of the service, and the actual export/receipt abroad.

  • Modelo DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) - customs export declaration with exit confirmation and NRE (Número de Referencia de Exportación)
  • Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR showing Spanish port/airport of exit and non-EU destination
  • Commercial invoice with Incoterm, full value, product/service description, destination, and export VAT exemption clause (Bienes exportados exentos - art. 21 LIVA)
  • Packing list and export licences for dual-use or restricted goods (if applicable)
  • Proof of payment / SWIFT MT103 (inward remittance) evidencing receipt of funds in the Spanish bank account of the SL
  • For cross-border services: signed contract, customer certificate of fiscal residence, and description of the actual place of use/benefit
  • Intrastat declarations when intra-EU dispatches exceed EUR 400,000 per calendar year

Real-time clearance via SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) is mandatory for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000, for VAT groups, and for non-established businesses using the EU refund procedure; SII requires electronic submission of invoice records to AEAT within 4 business days via web services/API (8 days for third-party issued invoices). All B2G invoicing uses Facturae format through FACe. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) will make electronic invoicing mandatory for all businesses after the implementing regulation is enacted, which is still pending; Regulation 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) mandates certified billing software with integrity, traceability and QR/hash features from 2025. Spain does not apply fiscal stamping or pre-clearance of individual invoices.

AEAT may retrospectively withdraw the 0% rate and assess 21% VAT on the invoice value plus late-payment interest if the export documentation is incomplete, the goods do not leave the EU, or the inward remittance is not received within the 180-day conformity period. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the VAT determined under arts. 170-171 LIVA, and the four-year limitation period allows clawback of prior periods. Falsifying export documents or creating fictitious exports may constitute a criminal offence under art. 305 Código Penal where the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1-5 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount; the tax assessment and penalty can be extended where concealment is shown, and the audit defence requires full availability of the DUA, transport evidence, payment evidence and contracts for the entire limitation period.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a euro-area member state and applies full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under EU Treaty principles and Royal Decree 1816/1991. The euro is freely convertible. There are no exchange-control restrictions on inward direct investment, foreign borrowing, or profit remittance. Dividends, interest, royalties, and liquidation proceeds may be repatriated through the Spanish banking system, subject only to standard tax documentation, corporate income tax/IRNR withholding obligations, transfer pricing substantiation, and AML/KYC verification. No prior Bank of Spain authorization is required for ordinary commercial payments.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Spain. Exporters and service providers are not required to convert foreign currency proceeds into euro, hold them in a designated account, or repatriate them within a statutory timeline. EU and Spanish law permit free retention and disposition of export proceeds in any permitted currency. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations and customs/foreign-transaction documentation may apply above the applicable reporting thresholds.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); for foreign-investment and statistical exchange-control matters, the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCEI) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation acts as the competent foreign-exchange administration.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, general rate, Ley 27/2014 art. 29.1)

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, art. 25.1.e TRLIRNR; rate set by Ley 5/2020). For EU/EEA shareholders holding at least 5% of the SL's capital for more than 12 consecutive months, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) provides a 0% withholding rate, subject to evidence of residence and no abuse. Domestic distributions to Spanish residents are subject to 19% personal income tax withholding at source.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

For a fiscal year ending 31 December, filing window runs from 1 to 25 July of the following year. General statutory rule: file within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax period end (art. 124 LIS). A foreign-owned SL with a permanent establishment in Spain files the same Modelo 200 on the PE's Spanish-sourced accounting results.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Instalments must be filed within the first 20 calendar days of April (first instalment), October (second instalment), and December (third instalment); for a calendar-year SL the first payment is due 1-20 April, the second 1-20 October, the third 1-20 December.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 00001 Declaration type code: '1' for ordinary declaration within the deadline, '3' for complementary declaration in response to a correction. Non-resident owner/shareholder: this box records the filer as the Spanish-resident entity; a non-resident PE branch files as a separate taxpayer with PE-specific code. Late filing without prior tax-office request triggers 'recargos por presentación extemporánea' under art. 27 LGT: 5% surcharge if the return is filed within 3 months after the deadline; 10% if within 3-6 months; 15% if within 6-12 months; and 20% plus late-payment interest if later. Where the tax authority formally requires the return first, the fine ranges from EUR 150 to EUR 6,000. Understatement leading to tax loss is characterised as a 'grave' infraction (art. 191 LGT) with a 50% penalty, or 100% with deliberate or proven concealment. Interest on late payment is 3.75% annually for the period of delay.
Box 00002 Taxpayer NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the SL. NIF must correspond to the Spanish entity's tax ID; non-resident companies operating through a PE use the PE's assigned NIF with suffix. Late filing without prior tax-office request triggers 'recargos por presentación extemporánea' under art. 27 LGT: 5% surcharge if the return is filed within 3 months after the deadline; 10% if within 3-6 months; 15% if within 6-12 months; and 20% plus late-payment interest if later. Where the tax authority formally requires the return first, the fine ranges from EUR 150 to EUR 6,000. Understatement leading to tax loss is characterised as a 'grave' infraction (art. 191 LGT) with a 50% penalty, or 100% with deliberate or proven concealment. Interest on late payment is 3.75% annually for the period of delay.
Box 00003 Corporate legal name (razón social) exactly as registered. For a PE, insert the foreign parent's name followed by 'Establecimiento Permanente en España'. Late filing without prior tax-office request triggers 'recargos por presentación extemporánea' under art. 27 LGT: 5% surcharge if the return is filed within 3 months after the deadline; 10% if within 3-6 months; 15% if within 6-12 months; and 20% plus late-payment interest if later. Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File and Master File are mandatory when the Spanish taxpayer's net turnover in the preceding tax period reaches EUR 45 million or the total related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period (arts. 18.3 and 18.8 LIS, RD 634/2015). Entities below these thresholds remain obliged to document each controlled transaction on a transactional file kept on request (art. 18.2 LIS). For a consumer-panel SaaS platform, the typical controlled transactions are: (i) payment processing fees charged by an Amazon/Wise/PayPal affiliate; (ii) data-cloud hosting services from a related entity; (iii) commission payments to affiliated market-research sub-contractors; and (iv) shareholder loans. All must be evidenced by policy-level documentation showing the pricing benchmark.

Economic substance scope: Spain applies no standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' in the Gulf-style sense, but the substance-over-form doctrine is codified in art. 15 LGT (conflicto en la aplicación de la norma tributaria), the general anti-abuse rule (art. 13? and GAAR), the CFC rules of arts. 100-108 LIS, and the principal-purpose test (PPT) included in OECD-based DTAs. A consumer-panel survey platform must demonstrate real economic substance in Spain: local headcount with research and data-analytics functions, local contracts with panel respondents, Spanish premises or sub-leased favourable space, actual decision-making on pricing and data processing, and bank accounts in Spain. Where an SL claims treaty benefits or the participation exemption on foreign dividends, AEAT may deny the benefit if the entity lacks sufficient substantive presence; in a Spanish court of law the burden of proving economic substance falls on the taxpayer. For holding companies of IP (not the case here), the ETVE regime (art. 21 LIS) additionally imposes a substance requirement of a minimum of one full-time director and an office in Spain.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion (delito contra la Hacienda Pública)

Statutory sanction: Prison sentence of 1 to 5 years plus a fine of six times the defrauded amount (arts. 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code). Where the fraud exceeds EUR 600,000 or the offence was committed through an organised network or false invoicing, the prison term is 2 to 6 years and the court may order closure of the business for up to 3 years.

Director personal liability: Directors of the SL who consent to or direct the concealment are personally liable as 'cooperadores necesarios' and jointly and severally liable for fines and civil restitution. Criminal courts may order disqualification from obtaining public subsidies, tax benefits or public contracts for up to 6 years, and they may impose a travel ban on EU/EEA movement? (preventive travel restriction) pending trial. Spanish criminal jurisdiction follows the foreign director if the offence is planned in Spain, and the legal entity itself may be prosecuted under art. 310 bis CP with penalties of up to 5 times the fine.
Shell company / abuse-of-law (conflicto en la aplicación de la norma)

Statutory sanction: AEAT recharacterises the transaction under art. 15 LGT, computing the tax due as legally applicable to the real substance and imposing a specific penalty of 50% of the resulting tax base (art. 206 bis LGT). Interest at 3.75% accrues on the recharacterisation amount. Aggravating circumstances may raise the penalty to 100%.

Director personal liability: Directors are derivatively liable for the tax debt when, acting in bad faith, they failed to exercise proper diligence in avoiding tax abuse (art. 43.2 LGT). In egregious cases, foreign directors may be barred from Spain's Golden Visa/Digital Nomad Visa regimes and may face a re-entry embargo for unpaid assessments.
Transfer pricing documentation failure and non-arm's-length pricing

Statutory sanction: AEAT assesses an upward taxation adjustment to the Spanish tax base plus 3.75% late-payment interest. Under art. 18.13 LIS, the penalty for absent or incomplete documentation is EUR 1,500 per data item or set of data with a minimum of EUR 15,000? (in practice, ERP practice); a deliberate manipulation of prices can involve the general infraction penalty of 50% of the adjustment (art. 191 LGT).

Director personal liability: The board of the SL bears personal residual liability if it authored the intercompany contracts that produced the tax base shift. Spanish jurisprudence has pierced the veil to attach the foreign parent's assets in Spain when the SL is domiciled, managed and controlled as a wholly owned instrument of a US/EU parent, making directors personally liable for the assessed difference.
Failure to withhold on outbound payments (IRNR)

Statutory sanction: The Spanish SL is substituted as the accountable taxpayer (retenedor) and AEAT requires payment of the unwithheld amounts plus interest and the full 50% infraction penalty under art. 191 LGT (or 100% in cases of concealment). A fine of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 may also be imposed per omitted form.

Director personal liability: Under art. 42.2.b) LGT, directors are jointly and severally liable in cases of wilful failure to withhold by a company that lacks sufficient assets to pay. A foreign director with assets in Spain (e.g., a bank account, a property or the shareholding of the SL) may face attachment and a prohibition on leaving Spain during the enforcement procedure.
AML and cash/illegal payment laundering (Ley 10/2010)

Statutory sanction: Financial and administrative infractions under Law 10/2010 carry fines up to EUR 150,000 for serious breaches and EUR 5,000,000 plus potential criminal consequences for money laundering under art. 301 CP (1 to 6 years' imprisonment and fines of treble the laundered value). The Bank of Spain may suspend the platform's operations for up to 3 years.

Director personal liability: Court-imposed travel bans, property embargoes and bank-account freezing orders are routine against directors of the SL; judges may order personal surrender of passports for repeat offenders. Since the platform uses PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, any flow of funds to sanctioned jurisdictions or to shells holding credentials causes immediate extraterritorial exposure and the SL's directors are personally exposed to anti-money-laundering enforcement from Spain's SEPBLAC and the criminal courts.
